problem: Unverified accounts now get role "". With require_role's new `in` check and the existing caller passing the plain string "admin", the check becomes `"" not in "admin"`, which is False. The empty string is a substring of every string, so unverified users pass the admin check. The change was meant to take privileges away and instead grants admin.
failure: POST /admin/purge with header `X-Auth-Token: t-new` (an unverified "user"): load_session sets role="", `"" not in "admin"` is False, no 403, and purge() runs. Before this change the request got a 403 because "user" != "admin".
fix: Fail closed for unverified users. Have require_role check `g.user["verified"]` and abort(403) when it is false, or use None as the no-role value. Also fix the substring matching in require_role (see the next finding).

problem: require_role changed from an equality check to `g.user["role"] not in roles`, but the existing caller api/admin.py:12 still passes the plain string "admin". So `in` does a substring test, and any role that is a substring of "admin" passes.
failure: An account with role "min", "ad", "dmi" or "" calls the view decorated with `@require_role("admin")`. `"min" not in "admin"` is False, so there is no 403 and the admin-only POST /admin/purge runs.
fix: Normalize roles: `if isinstance(roles, str): roles = (roles,)`, or switch to `*roles`. Or update api/admin.py to `@require_role(("admin",))` and reject str arguments.

problem: The require_role signature changed from a single role to a collection of roles, but nothing validates or normalizes the argument and the existing caller was not updated. The new contract breaks every current `@require_role("x")` call without any error.
failure: api/admin.py:12 `@require_role("admin")` now does substring matching without raising, so every `@require_role("<str>")` call has the same bypass.
fix: Reject or wrap a str argument at the decorator boundary, and update the call sites.

problem: The authorization behavior changed in both the decorator and the session role, and no test was added. CLAUDE.md requires a risk-proportionate test for behavior changes.
failure: No test covers `t-new` → POST /admin/purge → expect 403. That test would fail on this branch with a 200 or a purge.
fix: Add tests: unverified user gets 403, role "min" gets 403, admin gets 200, verified "user" gets 403.
